actor: AI national-security policy drafter, executive branch interagency working group
job: Assembling sanctions listings, procurement pressure and informal guidance into restrictions on specific named Chinese models rather than a categorical open-weights ban.
outcome: Named-model guidance reaching vendors and federal buyers while stopping short of any possession or download prohibition.
motivation: Chinese open models still trail Western ones on cybersecurity benchmarks, so a categorical instrument is judged unnecessary and legally costly.

task.who: Interagency AI and export-control policy staff
task.what: Assemble named-model restrictions short of a categorical ban
task.where: Interagency policy process and agency guidance documents
task.why: Categorical instruments carry legal and constitutional exposure
task.how: Entity listings, procurement signalling, informal vendor engagement

actor: Federal acquisition policy drafter, agency AI procurement office
job: Writing model-provenance and country-of-origin clauses into AI service solicitations so vendors must attest which models they serve on federal work.
outcome: Contract language making service of a named Chinese open-weight model incompatible with holding the federal award.
motivation: Procurement is the only lever that binds a counterparty; a self-hoster has no contract to condition.

task.who: Acquisition policy and contract clause drafting staff
task.what: Draft model-provenance attestation clauses for AI solicitations
task.where: Agency acquisition regulations and cloud contract vehicles
task.why: Only contracted vendors can be bound by conditions
task.how: Clause language, vendor attestations, contracting-officer guidance memos

actor: Cloud-catalog model-governance lead, US hyperscaler platform
job: Rewriting catalog listing criteria to screen third-party open-weight models by publisher jurisdiction, and drafting the public statement covering named exclusions.
outcome: A published catalog policy naming a specific Chinese open-weight model the platform will not serve, citing national-security concerns.
motivation: Federal contracts and enterprise customers demand a written provenance position, and silence about a named model is not sellable.

task.who: Model catalog governance and partner onboarding team
task.what: Publish named-model exclusions in the catalog listing policy
task.where: Public cloud model catalog policy and model cards
task.why: Federal and enterprise buyers require a written position
task.how: Publisher-jurisdiction screening, legal review, published policy pages

actor: Policy counsel, US-incorporated inference hosting provider
job: Reviewing hosted third-party open-weight models against federal guidance and drafting the public statement declining to serve named Chinese ones.
outcome: A public provider statement that it does not and will not serve a specific named Chinese open-weight model.
motivation: The company holds or wants federal business and needs a defensible published position before an agency or customer asks.

task.who: Legal, policy and model-onboarding review team
task.what: Publish a refusal to serve named Chinese models
task.where: Provider model list, terms of service and blog
task.why: Federal business needs a defensible published position
task.how: Guidance review, counsel sign-off, public policy posting

actor: Open-weights release lead, Chinese frontier model laboratory
job: Publishing full checkpoints under redistribution-permissive licenses on public hubs, without advance notice to US agencies or limits on third-party mirroring.
outcome: Named models whose weights and derivatives are lawfully redistributable, leaving no cooperating publisher for advance-review mechanisms to bind.
motivation: Permissive release buys adoption and standing abroad, and the lab sits outside the reach of US pre-release review programs.

task.who: Model release, licensing and community engagement teams
task.what: Publish checkpoints under permissive redistribution licenses
task.where: Public international model hubs and code repositories
task.why: Adoption depends on unrestricted third-party redistribution
task.how: Apache 2.0 license, public repository, model card

actor: Community quantization publisher, independent open-weights converter
job: Converting newly released Chinese open-weight checkpoints to quantized formats and re-uploading them to public hubs under the permissive upstream license.
outcome: Quantized derivatives of the named model staying fetchable from US-accessible hosts independent of the publisher's own repository.
motivation: Demand for single-card runnable weights far exceeds demand for the reference repository, and the license affirmatively permits re-upload.

task.who: Individual converters and small quantization collectives
task.what: Publish quantized conversions within days of each release
task.where: Public model hubs and community mirror repositories
task.why: Most users fetch derivatives, not reference repositories
task.how: GGUF conversion, calibration runs, permissively licensed re-upload

actor: Content-policy lead, US-accessible model hosting platform
job: Setting takedown criteria that act on published legal instruments and license violations rather than informal government preference or press reporting.
outcome: Named Chinese weights and their derivatives staying downloadable because no published instrument obliges the platform to remove them.
motivation: Removing lawfully licensed weights without a legal basis breaks trust with contributors and sets a precedent the platform cannot control.

task.who: Trust and safety, legal and repository policy team
task.what: Require a published legal instrument before removing weights
task.where: Platform content policy and repository moderation workflow
task.why: Informal preference is not a basis for removal
task.how: Documented takedown thresholds, counsel review, license verification
